title: Yosef ben Elam of Tzippori
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: [Yoma 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.12b) and [Megillah 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.9b) relate that a disqualification befell the High Priest (before Yom Kippur), and Yosef ben Elam was appointed in his place. Later, when the original High Priest returned, the Sages said that Yosef ben Elam was neither High Priest nor an ordinary priest. [Horayot 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.12b) gives his name as Yosef ben Ilim. In the Yerushalmi, Yoma, chapter 1, he appears simply as “ben Ilam of Tzipporin.”[^1]

notes.text: The parenthetical timing before Yom Kippur is Hyman’s. His parenthetic שיוסף ב״א abbreviates the same Yosef ben Elam already named, so the expansion adds no new patronymic. The variants אלם, אילים and אילם are kept distinct as Elam, Ilim and Ilam; the place-name spelling מציפורין is represented as Tzipporin in the final citation. Hyman’s exact Yerushalmi locator is פ״א ה״אד:; the earlier “halakhah ad” was an arbitrary parse and is withdrawn. No specific modern halakhah/folio conversion is asserted. The Bavli colon labels conventionally give 12b, 9b and 12b; these passages were not independently checked.
